content.recommendation: Exclusively breastfeed infants from birth until the completion of six months (180 days)[cite: 1025, 1027].
content.maternal_support: Mothers able to exclusively breastfeed until 180 days should be encouraged and supported to do so[cite: 1026].
content.benefits: Provides all nutrient needs for full-term infants of normal birth weight, reduces diarrhea and respiratory infections, and enhances motor and cognitive development[cite: 1028, 1029, 1030].

content.start_time: Introduce complementary foods immediately upon completion of 6 months[cite: 1025].
content.early_introduction_risk: Introduction before four months (120 days) is harmful as the child is physiologically and developmentally unready[cite: 1036].
content.delayed_introduction_risk: Delaying beyond six months adversely impacts nutrition, growth, and the ability to consume family foods by age one[cite: 1037].

content.storage_room_temp: Expressed Breast Milk (EBM) can be kept at room temperature for 8 hours[cite: 1042].
content.storage_refrigerated: EBM can be stored in a refrigerator for 24 hours[cite: 1042].
content.storage_frozen: EBM can be stored in a freezer compartment for 3 months[cite: 1042].
content.feeding_method: Feed EBM using a clean cup or a cup and a tea spoon[cite: 1043].

content.initial_texture: Always introduce complementary foods in a thick form from the beginning to provide more energy in smaller quantities[cite: 1048].
content.energy_boost: Use 1-2 teaspoons of oil when preparing food to increase energy density[cite: 1053].
content.consistency_progression: Start with soft semi-solid paste at 6 months and introduce coarsely mashed foods by the end of the 7th month[cite: 1113, 1114].

content.frequency: 2-3 meals per day plus frequent breast feeds[cite: 1056].
content.portion_size: Start with 2-3 teaspoons per feed, increasing gradually to slightly more than 1/2 a tea cup at each meal[cite: 1056].
content.snacks: 1-2 snacks may be offered depending on the child's appetite[cite: 1056].

content.texture: Coarsely chopped or mashed foods and finger foods[cite: 1056].
content.portion_size: About 3/4 of a tea cup at each meal[cite: 1056].

content.texture: Family foods, chopped or mashed coarsely if necessary[cite: 1056].
content.frequency: 3-4 meals plus breast milk given after meals[cite: 1056].
content.portion_size: 1 tea cup or slightly more at each meal[cite: 1056].

content.animal_sources: Include fish, sprats, poultry, meat, and liver daily from the beginning of the 7th month[cite: 1067, 1068].
content.vegetarian_sources: Gotukola, Sarana, Thampala, Soya, green gram, and cowpea[cite: 1069].
content.absorption_booster: Include Vitamin C sources like lemon, lime, nelli, guava, banana, or papaya in the same meal to increase iron bioavailability[cite: 1070].

content.food_sources: Liver, egg yolk, yellow pumpkin, yellow sweet potatoes, carrots, papaw, mangoes, and dark green leaves[cite: 1075].
content.mega_dose_infant: 100,000 IU given at 9 months (with measles vaccine), 18 months, and 3 years[cite: 1123].
content.mega_dose_maternal: Postpartum mothers receive 200,000 IU within two weeks of delivery[cite: 1127].

content.egg_yolk: Can be introduced from the 7th month; must be well cooked (boiled or fried firm)[cite: 1076].
content.egg_white: Can be introduced from the 9th month[cite: 1077].
content.benefit: Eggs are a cheap source of good quality protein and can be given daily[cite: 1077].

content.autonomy: Encourage children to self-feed reaching two years[cite: 1023, 1096].
content.interaction: Talk lovingly during feeding and maintain eye contact[cite: 1100].
content.patience: Feed children patiently and avoid forced feeding at all times[cite: 1097, 1098].

content.hand_washing: Caregivers must wash hands with soap before preparation and feeding; children's hands must be washed before eating[cite: 1107].
content.bottles: Avoid the use of feeding bottles[cite: 1110].
content.utensils: Use clean cups, bowls, and spoons dedicated to the child[cite: 1109].

content.during_illness: Increase fluid intake and frequency of breastfeeding; offer small, energy-dense favorite foods frequently (every 2-3 hours)[cite: 1141, 1143, 1144].
content.after_illness: Provide one extra meal daily for at least 2 weeks after recovery to maintain growth[cite: 1138, 1139].
content.symptom_management: Manage symptoms like fever before offering food as a feverish child will refuse it[cite: 18].

content.weighing_infant: Weigh children monthly up to two years (24 months)[cite: 1148].
content.weighing_child: Weigh every three months from age two up to five years[cite: 1148].
content.length_height: Measure length at 4, 9, and 18 months; measure height every 6 months after age two[cite: 1152].

content.definition: A small quantity of energy-dense food or drink taken between main meals that is quick to prepare[cite: 1175].
content.examples_infant: Yoghurt, curd, bread with butter/margarine, boiled gram, thriposha, or fruits[cite: 1177, 1082].
content.traditional_snacks: Helapa, sago pudding, weli thalapa, and aggala can be given after one year[cite: 1178].

content.rice_cereal: 1/2 a tea cup of cooked rice or cereal equals one serving[cite: 1182].
content.bread: 1 slice of bread (450g loaf cut into 9 slices) equals one serving[cite: 1183].
content.potatoes: 2 egg-sized potatoes or 1 egg-sized sweet potato equals one serving[cite: 1185, 1186].

content.meat_fish: 25-50g of cooked fish/chicken/meat (size of a matchbox) or 6 sprats equals one serving[cite: 1199].
content.milk_powder: 3 heaped teaspoons of milk powder equals one serving[cite: 1193].
content.cheese: A match-box-sized piece of cheese equals one serving[cite: 1192].

content.infant_use: Provided to infants with growth faltering or underweight from 6 months until one year[cite: 1121].
content.maternal_use: Breastfeeding mothers receive Thriposha for a minimum of six months[cite: 1126].

content.preterm_lbw_start: Begin iron supplementation from two months of age[cite: 1131, 1132].
content.duration: Continue until at least one year, preferably up to 2 years[cite: 1132].

content.choking_hazards: Avoid small, rounded, hard pieces of vegetables and whole nuts or pulses[cite: 1086].
content.blending_warning: Avoid blending or straining food after 8 months to encourage munching skills[cite: 1087, 1022].
content.finger_foods: Introduce items like hoppers (soft center) or thin fruit slices around 8-9 months[cite: 1115].

content.daily_supplements: Iron, folic acid, Vitamin C, and Calcium for at least six months postpartum[cite: 1126].
content.vitamin_a_maternal: 200,000 IU mega dose within two weeks of delivery[cite: 1127].

content.salt_sugar: Avoid adding salt or sugar to food during the first year[cite: 1085, 2].
content.honey: Do not add honey to curd or other foods[cite: 1083].

content.sprat_prep: Wash sprats whole (with head), air/oven dry, and grind whole to a fine texture; add one teaspoon to meals[cite: 5].
content.iron_importance: Iron-rich animal foods are essential for rapid brain development in the first two years[cite: 5].

content.meal_amount: Slightly more than 1/2 tea cup of coarsely chopped food, 3-4 times a day[cite: 12].
content.social_interaction: Encourage the baby to sit with family members during meal times[cite: 1104, 12].

content.daily_fish_meat: Two pieces the size of a match-box[cite: 15].

content.daily_milk_products: 1 cup of curd or yogurt per day[cite: 15].
content.daily_vegetables: 3 - 6 tablespoons of mixed vegetables plus 1/2 tea cup of green leaves[cite: 15].
content.daily_fruit: Fruits given twice a day (e.g., one medium banana and one orange)[cite: 15].

content.medical_oversight: Introduction of formula milk should only be decided by a doctor[cite: 21].
content.long_term_risks: Formula milk in the first year can have adverse long-term health effects[cite: 21].
content.daily_limit_1_5yrs: Raw amount for formula-fed infants is 400ml/day for the 1-5 year age group[cite: 1091].

content.meal_composition: Coarsely mashed rice with pulses, iron-rich animal foods, eggs, vegetables, and green leaves[cite: 9].
content.importance: Various types of food and different tastes ensure nutrient needs are met and healthy eating habits develop[cite: 9].

content.distractions: Minimize distractions; have a separate place to feed the child[cite: 1103, 2].
content.hunger_satiety: Caregivers should be sensitive to the child's hunger and satiety cues[cite: 1097].
content.eye_contact: Maintain eye-to-eye contact to encourage eating while stimulating brain development[cite: 2, 1100].

content.stunting_prev: 13.5% of children under five are stunted[cite: 1011].
content.underweight_prev: 29.4% of children under five are underweight[cite: 1011].
content.anaemia_prev: Nearly 30% of children under five suffer from iron deficiency anaemia[cite: 1013].

content.nutritional_need: Required to meet increasing needs that breast milk alone cannot provide[cite: 1021].
content.munching_skill: Trains the child to eat different tastes/consistencies to transition to family foods[cite: 1022].
content.self_feeding_skill: Stimulates development-appropriate feeding skills for self-feeding by age two[cite: 1023].

content.day_1: 2-3 teaspoons of very well mashed rice mixed with expressed breast milk[cite: 3].
content.day_2_3: One or two meals a day of very well mashed rice, gradually increasing the amount[cite: 3].

content.additions: Start adding pulses such as dhal to the rice[cite: 4].
content.portion: 3-4 teaspoons at a time, twice a day[cite: 4].
content.fruit_intro: One teaspoon of well mashed fruit (e.g., papaya, banana) after the rice meal[cite: 4].

content.cooked_fruit_veg: 3 tablespoons of cooked fruit vegetables (e.g., pumpkin, carrot) equals one serving[cite: 1202].
content.leafy_greens: 1/2 a tea cup of cooked leafy vegetables equals one serving[cite: 1203].
content.fresh_fruit: 1 medium banana or orange equals one serving[cite: 1200].

content.yellow_pages: Parents should read the yellow pages in the CHDR for feeding guidance[cite: 21].
content.consultation: Ask the Public Health Midwife or doctor to explain unclear points[cite: 21].
content.uniformity: Guidelines ensure uniformity in nutrition messages given by all health personnel[cite: 1019].

content.stunting_peak: Nutritional problems in Sri Lanka typically appear around the sixth month and rise steadily into the second year[cite: 1018].
content.primary_cause: Incorrect complementary feeding practices are identified as a major cause for undernutrition in this age group[cite: 1018].
content.impact: Early nutritional insults lead to reduced adult IQ, work capacity, and national development[cite: 1016, 1017].

content.self_feeding_goal: Children should be trained to eat on their own by the age of two[cite: 1023, 1096].
content.munching_skill: Introduction of complementary foods at 6 months helps train children to munch, easing the transition to family foods by age one[cite: 1022].
content.manual_dexterity: Allowing children to touch food with washed hands encourages sensory learning[cite: 1099].

content.anaemia_prevalence: Nearly 30% of children under five in Sri Lanka suffer from iron deficiency anaemia[cite: 1013].
content.critical_sources: Iron-rich foods like liver, sprats, meat, and fish should be introduced early (from the 7th month)[cite: 1067, 1068].
content.cognitive_link: Iron is essential for rapid brain development which is fastest in the first two years of life.

content.sprat_cleaning: Wash sprats whole without removing the head.
content.processing: Air dry, oven dry, or roast the sprats before grinding them whole to a fine texture.
content.storage: Store the sprat powder in a clean bottle and add about one teaspoon to the baby's meal.

content.fat_additives: Temper food with 1-2 teaspoons of oil or butter[cite: 1053, 1078].
content.local_energy_source: Cook food with thick coconut milk to increase energy content.
content.rationale: Small stomach capacities in infants require energy-dense foods to meet growth needs[cite: 1048, 1059].

content.mix_standard: Rice should be mixed with a pulse (dhal/green gram) and animal food (liver/meat/sprats).
content.vegetable_inclusion: Add yellow vegetables like pumpkin, carrot, or yellow sweet potatoes.
content.serving_frequency: Offer 5-6 teaspoons at a time, twice a day.

content.local_greens: Introduce Gotukola, Murunga leaves, Sarana, Thampala, or Mukunuwenna.
content.meal_rotation: Give different items at different meals (e.g., Gotukola for lunch, Sarana for dinner).
content.portion: Amount given should be about 1/4 of a tea cup, 2-3 times a day.

content.texture_milestone: Transition to coarsely mashed rice upon completion of the 7th month.
content.portion_increase: Give 1/2 tea cup at a time, 2-3 times a day.
content.snack_introduction: Offer well-mashed fruit as a snack in between meals.

content.food_diversity: Introduce local staples like Jak and breadfruit.
content.portion: Give slightly more than 1/2 tea cup of food at a time, 2-3 times a day.
content.fruit_portion: Provide scraped fruit (about 1/4 tea cup) between main meals.

content.local_finger_foods: Offer a small piece of hopper (soft center portion) or bread with butter.
content.fruit_slices: Ripe avocado or other soft scraped fruit can be given as finger food.
content.supervision_rule: The baby must never be left alone with finger foods due to choking risks.

content.meal_pattern: Give a bit more than 1/2 tea cup of coarsely chopped food, 3-4 times a day.
content.social_inclusion: Try to let the baby sit with family members during meal times.
content.breastfeeding_sequence: Breastfeed after meals rather than before.

content.serving_method: Rice and 'curries' can be served separately and mixed while feeding.
content.portion: 3/4 tea cup of food at a time, 3-4 times a day.
content.self_feeding: Encourage the child to touch and pick up foods independently.

content.diet_milestone: The child should be consuming nutritious family foods.
content.meal_count: Three main meals a day, with portions slightly larger than one tea cup.
content.daily_diversity: Aim to include 5 different items of vegetables and fruits daily.

content.protein_visual: Two matchbox-sized pieces of fish, chicken, meat, or liver per day.
content.seafood_local: 2 tablespoons of Kunissan (small shrimp) equals the daily protein requirement.
content.sprats_count: 6 - 8 sprats per day for a child aged 1-2 years.

content.dairy_units: 1 cup of curd or yogurt daily.
content.breast_milk: Give 2-3 times a day, ideally after a meal.

content.snack_purpose: Snacks provide extra energy and nutrients in small amounts.
content.frequency_logic: Offer 1-2 snacks a day based on the baby's hunger cues and weight gain.
content.example: A piece of boiled potato with butter or a piece of boiled egg.

content.intro_timeline: Start eggs 2 weeks after beginning complementary feeding.
content.sequence: Feed a little boiled egg yolk first, followed by boiled egg white about one week later.
content.affordability: Eggs are a less expensive source of nutritious food that can be served daily.

content.fever_management: Control symptoms like fever before feeding, as a feverish child will refuse food.
content.patience: Feed an ill child with extra patience and love in small, frequent amounts.
content.recovery_diet: Provide an extra meal and extra breastfeeds for about 2 weeks after recovery.

content.weighing_monthly: Weigh the child every month until their 2nd birthday.
content.clinical_records: Mark all measurements in the Child Health Development Record (CHDR).

content.growth_faltering: If a child has growth faltering, underweight, or overweight, seek special advice from healthcare staff.
content.formula_milk_warning: Formula milk is discouraged and should only be used on a doctor's recommendation.
content.chdr_resources: Parents should utilize the yellow pages in the CHDR for detailed guidance.

content.mealtime_learning: During meals, point out and name different foods, show various colors, and discuss tastes.
content.brain_stim: Active engagement during meals stimulates learning and brain development.
content.emotional_bond: Talking lovingly encourages the baby to love meal times.

content.postpartum_dose: Mothers receive 200,000 IU within two weeks of delivery or before discharge[cite: 1127].
content.infant_mega_dose: 100,000 IU is given at 9, 18, and 36 months[cite: 1123].
content.safety_interval: Avoid supplements containing Vitamin A if a mega dose was received in the last 6 months[cite: 1124].

content.lbw_start: Low birth weight and preterm infants start iron supplements from two months of age[cite: 1131].
content.dosage_rule: Standard iron dosage is 2mg per kg of body weight daily[cite: 1129].
content.community_dose: In community programs, 12.5mg of elemental iron daily is recommended for 2 months[cite: 1130].

content.prep_speed: Serve food immediately after preparation and keep it well-covered[cite: 1108].
content.utensil_integrity: Child-specific cups and bowls should not be used for any other purpose[cite: 1109].
content.hydration: Offer boiled, cooled water to the baby after meals.

content.raw_amount_cereals: Daily requirement for children aged 1-5 is 230g of cereals[cite: 1091].
content.cup_volume: A standard tea cup for measurement in Sri Lanka is 200ml[cite: 1056, 1204].
content.bread_standard: A 450g loaf of bread should be cut into 9 slices for standardized serving sizes[cite: 1183].

content.daily_fish_meat_grams: 50g per day raw weight for fish or meat[cite: 1091].
content.daily_pulses_grams: 60g per day raw weight for lentils, pulses, or nuts[cite: 1091].
content.daily_fruit_grams: 100g per day raw weight for fruits[cite: 1091].

content.daily_veg_grams: 50g per day raw weight for vegetables[cite: 1091].
content.daily_greens_grams: 50g per day raw weight for green leafy vegetables[cite: 1091].
content.daily_sugar_limit: 25g per day raw weight limit for sugar[cite: 1091].

content.hunger_cues: Feed infants by being sensitive to hunger and satiety (fullness) cues[cite: 1097].
content.no_force: Forced feeding must be discouraged at all times[cite: 1098].
content.experimentation: If food is refused, experiment with different combinations and preparations[cite: 1101, 1102].

content.yellow_produce: Yellow pumpkin, yellow sweet potatoes, and carrots are rich in Vitamin A[cite: 1075].
content.yolk_timing: Egg yolk can be introduced from the seventh month[cite: 1076].
content.white_timing: Egg white should be introduced from the ninth month[cite: 1077].

content.iron_boost: Adding Vitamin C sources like lemon or lime to vegetarian meals increases iron absorption[cite: 1070].
content.citrus_prep: When giving orange or mandarin, a minimal amount of water can be added[cite: 1074].
content.water_offering: Sips of boiled, cooled water can be offered after meals starting at 6 months.
